correctness.rationale: For every a,b>0 the exact stroboscopic map is increasing and bounded, with G(x)-x equal to negative x times the explicit quartic divided by a positive denominator. Its positive zeros correspond to intersections of a strictly convex coercive scalar B_a with horizontal level b, proving precisely zero, one double or two simple positive roots. The exact Sylvester discriminant identity Disc(Q)=-a^4 H, and the fact that H as a quadratic in b^2 has exactly one positive zero, identify signs and all parameter boundaries. Strict sign intervals and monotone bounded iteration prove every global basin and tangency case. The factorization H=(ab-4)(3ab+4)^3-256(a-b)^2 proves contrast threshold and symmetric dependence; a direct AM-GM bound ab>=4 for any positive cycle checks the critical boundary. Exact rational arithmetic and resultant checker passed 445 assertions (limited finite diagnostics).

originality.rationale: The precise positive-two-season-state trichotomy, complete all-initial-data basins, symmetric degree-eight boundary and fixed-geometric-mean contrast cutoff are not statements established by the most relevant inspected source materials. Closest primary literature develops general Allee frameworks and other specific maps; a related 2010 paper is unimodal, unlike the strictly increasing sigmoid response. Relevant mathematical indexing records describe cubic Allee maps, different periodically forced population projections and seasonal Ricker maps, not this sharp parameter boundary. Priority is provisional given unexamined older literature, but no concrete broader result was found that implies this exact claim.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible earlier work may contain the same special-case algebra or a direct implication; no independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The result identifies a previously unaccounted-for sharp dependence of conditional persistence on seasonal contrast in a biologically motivated Allee response. A fixed positive geometric-mean reproduction value is insufficient to predict survival; exact parameters (1,9) and (1/4,36) have the same product but opposite long-term fates. The theorem classifies every initial population and all equality cases, so it is not merely a numerical example or a routine local stability test. Its utility is an exact model benchmark, not unsubstantiated empirical significance.
